weeks.title: Inside a Computer and Your First C Program
weeks.summary: Is week aap samjhoge ki CPU aur memory milkar program kaise chalate hain, machine level par loop aur branch kaise bante hain, aur apna pehla C program likh kar chalaoge.
concepts: **CPU** computer ka dimaag hai. Isme **ALU** (arithmetic aur logic operations), **registers** (bahut tez, chhoti storage) aur **control unit** hote hain. CPU baar-baar ek hi cycle chalata hai: instruction **fetch** karo, **decode** karo, **execute** karo.

**Memory (RAM)** bytes ki ek lambi line hai. Har byte ka ek number hota hai jise **address** kehte hain. Agar address n bits ka hai to 2ⁿ alag bytes tak pahunch sakte hain, jaise 16-bit address se 65,536 bytes (64 KB). RAM volatile hai, power gayi to data gaya.

**Stored-program idea**: program ke instructions aur data dono memory mein rakhe jaate hain. CPU ka **Program Counter (PC)** register agle instruction ka address rakhta hai. Har fetch ke baad PC normally agle instruction par chala jaata hai.

**Branch aur loop machine level par**: ek **jump** instruction PC ko kisi naye address par set kar deta hai. **Conditional jump** (jaise "agar register zero nahi hai to jump karo") se `if` banta hai, aur peeche ki taraf jump karne se **loop** banta hai.

**I/O (Input/Output)**: keyboard, screen, disk jaise devices se data aata-jaata hai. Inko seedha program nahi chalata, **operating system (OS)** sambhalta hai. C mein `printf` text ko standard output (screen) par bhejta hai.

**Programming language aur C**: CPU sirf machine code (0 aur 1) samajhta hai. Hum C jaisi high-level language mein likhte hain aur **compiler** usse machine code mein badalta hai. C hardware ke kaafi paas hai, isliye OS, embedded systems aur drivers mein bahut use hota hai.

**Pehla C program**: `#include <stdio.h>` se `printf` ki declaration milti hai, `int main(void)` se program shuru hota hai, har statement `;` par khatam hota hai, aur `return 0;` OS ko batata hai ki program theek se khatam hua. `\n` naya line deta hai.

example.problem: Neeche wala program kya print karega, aur har line ka kaam kya hai?
steps: `#include <stdio.h>`: preprocessor standard I/O header ko jodta hai, jisme `printf` declared hai.
`int main(void)`: har C program yahin se chalna shuru hota hai. `void` ka matlab hai koi argument nahi.
`printf("Hello, C!\n");`: quotes ke andar ka text print hota hai, aur `\n` cursor ko agli line par le jaata hai.
`return 0;`: main se 0 wapas OS ko jaata hai, matlab "sab theek raha".
Curly braces `{ }` main ki body ko gherte hain.
Answer: screen par **Hello, C!** aata hai aur cursor agli line par chala jaata hai.

mistakes: Statement ke end mein `;` bhool jaana. Compiler agli line par error dikhata hai, isliye error wali line se ek line upar bhi dekho.
`Printf` ya `Main` likhna. C case-sensitive hai, sahi naam `printf` aur `main` hain.
`\n` bhool jaana. Tab agla output usi line par chipak jaata hai. Jahan nayi line chahiye wahan `\n` lagao.
revision: CPU cycle: fetch → decode → execute.
PC = agle instruction ka address; jump instruction PC badal deta hai.
n-bit address → 2ⁿ bytes tak memory.
Instructions aur data dono memory mein (stored-program).
Compiler: C source → machine code. Har C program `main` se shuru hota hai.

questions.question: Stored-program computer mein kaunsa register **agle** instruction ka address rakhta hai?
questions.explanation: Program Counter (PC) agle instruction ka address rakhta hai; fetch ke baad woh aage badh jaata hai aur jump instruction use naya address de deta hai. Trap: Instruction Register, par woh abhi chal rahe (fetch ho chuke) instruction ko rakhta hai, agle ka address nahi.

questions.question: Is program ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Har `printf` apne aap nayi line nahi deta. "IIT" ke turant baad "M" chipakta hai, phir `\n` se line badalti hai, aur "BS" doosri line par aata hai. Trap: har `printf` ko alag line maan lena (teen lines wala option).

questions.question: Ek toy CPU ka program memory mein address 100 se rakha hai. HALT par pahunchne ke baad R1 mein kya value hogi?
questions.explanation: Trace karo: R1 = 0, R2 = 3. Pehli baar ADD se R1 = 3, R2 = 2, jump. Doosri baar R1 = 5, R2 = 1, jump. Teesri baar R1 = 6, R2 = 0, ab JNZ jump nahi karta aur HALT aata hai. Answer 6 (3 + 2 + 1). Trap: 9, yeh maan kar ki R2 hamesha 3 hi rehta hai; ya 5, ek round pehle ruk jaana.

questions.question: Ek computer mein memory address 16 bits ka hai aur har address ek byte ko point karta hai. Yeh computer zyada se zyada kitni bytes memory address kar sakta hai?
questions.explanation: 16 bits se 2¹⁶ = 65,536 alag patterns bante hain, har pattern ek address, to 65,536 bytes = 64 KB. Trap: 32,768 (2¹⁵), yeh signed number ki range wali soch hai; addresses hamesha unsigned hote hain. 16 bytes bits ko hi bytes samajhna hai.

questions.question: Is program ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `return 0;` chalte hi `main` khatam ho jaata hai, isliye uske baad wala `printf("end\n")` kabhi execute nahi hota. Sirf "start" print hota hai. Return ke baad code likhna error nahi hai (bas unreachable code hai), isliye compile error wala option galat hai.

questions.question: Is toy program mein HALT samet kul kitne instructions execute honge, aur end mein R2 kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 2 LOAD chalte hain. Loop round 1: ADD (R2 = 4), SUB (R1 = 2), JNZ jump karta hai. Round 2: ADD (R2 = 6), SUB (R1 = 0), JNZ jump nahi karta. Phir HALT. Kul 2 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 9 instructions, R2 = 6. Trap: 6, har line ko ek hi baar ginna (loop dobara chalta hai yeh bhool jaana); 12, loop ko R1 = 0 par bhi ek baar aur chala dena.

questions.question: CPU har instruction ke liye kaunsa cycle sahi order mein chalata hai?
questions.explanation: CPU pehle memory se instruction laata hai (**fetch**), phir samajhta hai ki kya karna hai (**decode**), aur phir kaam karta hai (**execute**). Trap: "fetch → execute → decode", par bina decode kiye CPU ko pata hi nahi ki execute kya karna hai; aur decode fetch se pehle ho hi nahi sakta, kyunki instruction abhi aaya hi nahi.

questions.question: Is program ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation:
Pehle `printf` mein do `
` hain: "Hi" ke baad line badalti hai, "there" ke baad phir badalti hai. Isliye doosre `printf` ka "!" teesri line par aata hai. Trap: "there!" ek saath maan lena, yeh bhool kar ki "there" ke baad bhi `
` hai; ya `
` ko hi ignore kar dena.

questions.question: Computer ki power achanak chali jaaye to kahan rakha data turant kho jaata hai?
questions.explanation: RAM **volatile** hai: data tabhi tak rehta hai jab tak power hai. Hard disk, SSD aur pen drive non-volatile storage hain, power jaane par bhi data bacha rehta hai. Trap: SSD ko RAM jaisa samajhna kyunki dono chips se bane hain; par SSD power ke bina bhi data rakhta hai.

questions.question: Ek computer mein 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes) memory hai aur har byte ka alag address chahiye. Address kam se kam kitne bits ka hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: n bits se 2ⁿ addresses bante hain. 2¹⁰ = 1024 (1 KB), to 2²⁰ = 1024 × 1024 = 1,048,576 (1 MB). Isliye 20 bits kaafi hain aur 19 kam padenge. Trap: 16 bits, jo sirf 64 KB tak jaata hai; 10 bits sirf 1 KB deta hai; 32 bits kaam to karega par "kam se kam" nahi hai.

questions.question: Is toy program ke HALT par pahunchne ke baad R2 mein kya value hogi?
questions.explanation: Loop body (302–304) tab tak chalti hai jab tak R1 zero na ho. R1 5 se shuru hota hai aur har round 1 ghatta hai, to body 5 baar chalti hai (R1 = 4, 3, 2, 1, 0). Har baar R2 mein 2 judta hai: 5 × 2 = 10. Trap: 8, R1 = 0 hone wale round ko na ginna (ADD us round mein SUB se pehle ho chuka hota hai); 12, ek round zyada; 2, jump ko ignore karna.

questions.question: HALT par R1 mein kya hoga, aur HALT samet kul kitne instructions execute honge?
questions.explanation: `ADD R1, R1` har round R1 ko double karta hai. R2 = 4 se loop 4 baar chalta hai: R1 = 2, 4, 8, 16. Instructions: 2 LOAD + 4 rounds × 3 (ADD, SUB, JNZ) + 1 HALT = 2 + 12 + 1 = 15. Trap: 6, har line ko ek hi baar ginna; "R1 = 8, 12", ek round kam chalana; "R1 = 32, 18", ek round zyada chalana.

questions.question: Yeh toy program machine level par if-else jaisa hai. Kaunse addresses kis order mein execute honge, aur HALT par R2 kya hoga?
questions.code:
500: LOAD R1, 0      ; R1 = 0
501: JNZ  R1, 504    ; if R1 != 0, jump to 504
502: LOAD R2, 7      ; R2 = 7
503: JMP  505        ; always jump to 505
504: LOAD R2, 9      ; R2 = 9
505: HALT
questions.explanation: R1 = 0 hai, isliye 501 par JNZ jump nahi karta aur PC normally 502 par jaata hai: R2 = 7. Phir 503 ka JMP bina condition ke PC ko 505 par bhej deta hai, to 504 skip hota hai. Order: 500, 501, 502, 503, 505 aur R2 = 7. Trap: JNZ ko "zero par jump" padhna (504 wala raasta); JMP ko bhool kar 504 bhi chala dena (R2 = 9 ho jaata); ya 503 ko gin hi na paana.

questions.question: Is program ka output screen par kaisa dikhega?
questions.explanation:
"ab" ke baad do `
` lagataar hain: pehla line khatam karta hai, doosra ek khaali line bana deta hai. "cd" ke baad newline nahi hai, isliye agle `printf` ka "e" usi line par chipakta hai: "cde". Phir `return 0;` se `main` khatam, to "f" kabhi print nahi hota. Trap: `

` ko ek hi newline maanna ("ab / cde"); har `printf` ko nayi line samajhna; ya return ke baad ka code bhi chala dena.

questions.question: Ek CPU mein har instruction 4 bytes leta hai aur program address 2000 se lagataar rakha hai (pehla instruction 2000 par). Koi jump nahi hai. 5th instruction kis address par hai, aur use fetch karne ke turant baad PC kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Instructions 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016 par hain, to 5th instruction 2000 + 4 × 4 = 2016 par hai (pehla instruction khud 2000 par hai, isliye 4 kadam, 5 nahi). Fetch ke baad PC agle instruction ka address rakhta hai: 2016 + 4 = 2020. Trap: 2020, 5 × 4 jod dena; 2004/2005, har instruction ko 1 byte maanna; PC = 2017, PC ko 1 se badhana jabki instruction 4 bytes ka hai.

weeks.title: Bits, Bytes and Data Representation
weeks.summary: Is week aap binary aur hex, two's complement se negative numbers, floating point ki basics, ASCII characters, instructions ki encoding, aur compiler aur OS ka role seekhoge.
concepts: **Binary aur hexadecimal**: computer sab kuch bits (0/1) mein rakhta hai. 8 bits = 1 byte. Hex base 16 hai (0–9, A–F) aur ek hex digit = 4 bits, isliye `0x2F` = 0010 1111 = 2·16 + 15 = 47. C mein hex likhne ke liye `0x` prefix lagta hai.
**Unsigned range**: n bits se 0 se 2ⁿ − 1 tak numbers bante hain. 8 bits: 0–255, 16 bits: 0–65535.

**Two's complement**: negative number banane ke liye saare bits ulto (invert) aur 1 jodo. Range −2ⁿ⁻¹ se 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, jaise 8-bit mein −128 se 127. Sabse left wala bit (MSB) 1 hai to number negative hai. Example: −5 = 1111 1011.

**Overflow**: fixed bits mein result fit na ho to bits wrap ho jaate hain. 8-bit hardware mein 127 + 1 ka bit pattern 1000 0000 = −128 banta hai. (C mein signed overflow undefined behaviour hai, isse kabhi rely mat karo.)

**Floating point (IEEE 754)**: number ko sign, exponent aur mantissa (fraction) mein rakha jaata hai. `float` 32 bits (~7 decimal digits), `double` 64 bits (~15–16 digits). 0.1 jaise numbers binary mein exact nahi bante, isliye floats ko `==` se compare karna risky hai.
**Characters aur ASCII**: `char` asal mein ek chhota integer hai. ASCII mein `'A'` = 65, `'a'` = 97, `'0'` = 48, aur letters/digits lagataar hote hain, isliye `'A' + 2` = `'C'` aur `'7' - '0'` = 7.

**Instruction encoding**: instructions bhi bit patterns hain. Ek instruction ke bits fields mein bante hain, jaise opcode (kaunsa kaam), register number aur immediate value. 4-bit opcode field ho to 2⁴ = 16 alag opcodes ho sakte hain.

**Compilation aur OS**: compiler C source ko machine code wali executable file mein badalta hai. Chalane par **OS** us file ko memory mein load karta hai, CPU time deta hai, aur I/O (screen, files) sambhalta hai.

example.problem: −20 ko 8-bit two's complement mein likho (binary aur hex dono).
steps: Pehle +20 ko binary mein likho: 20 = 16 + 4, to 0001 0100.
Saare bits invert karo: 1110 1011.
4-4 bits ke group se hex: 1110 = E, 1100 = C, to 0xEC.
Check: 0xEC unsigned 236 hai, aur 236 − 256 = −20 ✓.

mistakes: Two's complement mein sirf bits invert karke ruk jaana. Woh one's complement hai; +1 jodna zaroori hai.
Negative number ko sign-magnitude ki tarah padhna (MSB = minus, baaki = value). 1111 1110 ka matlab −126 nahi, −2 hai.
`'5'` (character, value 53) aur `5` (integer) ko same samajhna. Digit character se number chahiye to `'5' - '0'` karo.
revision: 1 hex digit = 4 bits; `0x` prefix hex batata hai.
Two's complement: invert + 1; 8-bit range −128 se 127.
`float` ~7 digits, `double` ~15–16 digits; 0.1 exact nahi hota.
Instruction = bit fields (opcode, register, immediate).

questions.question: Hexadecimal number `0x3A` ki decimal value kya hai?
questions.explanation: `0x3A` = 3·16 + A, aur A = 10, to 48 + 10 = 58. Trap: 310, digits ko decimal ki tarah jod dena ("3" aur "10"); 40, base 16 ki jagah base 10 use karna (3·10 + 10); 13, digits ko bas add kar dena.

questions.question: 8-bit two's complement mein bit pattern 1111 1110 kis number ko dikhata hai?
questions.explanation: MSB 1 hai, to number negative hai. Magnitude nikalne ke liye invert + 1: 0000 0001 + 1 = 0000 0010 = 2, to value −2. Trap: −126, isse sign-magnitude ki tarah padhna; 254, unsigned value; −1, woh 1111 1111 hota hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga? (ASCII maan kar)
questions.code:
char ch = 'A' + 2;
printf("%c %d\n", ch, ch);
questions.explanation: `'A'` ki ASCII value 65 hai, 65 + 2 = 67, jo `'C'` hai. `%c` same value ko character ki tarah (C) aur `%d` number ki tarah (67) dikhata hai. Trap: "C 65", yeh sochna ki `%d` original 'A' ki value dikhayega; ya +2 ko ek hi letter aage samajhna (B 66).

questions.question: 16-bit two's complement integer ki range kya hai?
questions.explanation: n bits ke liye range −2ⁿ⁻¹ se 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1 hai. n = 16: −32768 se 32767. Negative side par ek number zyada hai kyunki zero positive side ki jagah leta hai. Trap: −32767 se 32767, yeh one's complement / sign-magnitude ki range hai (jisme do zero hote hain); 0 se 65535 unsigned range hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 0.1 binary mein exact nahi banta. `0.1f` float (24-bit mantissa) mein round hota hai, lagbhag 0.100000001490116, jabki `0.1` ek double hai jo 0.1000000000000000055 ke kareeb hai. Comparison ke liye f ko double banaya jaata hai, par value wahi float wali rehti hai, isliye dono alag hain: "not equal". Trap: maths mein dono 0.1 hain, isliye "equal" lagna.

questions.question: Ek toy CPU ke 16-bit instruction mein upar ke 4 bits opcode, agle 4 bits register number, aur neeche ke 8 bits ek unsigned immediate value hain. Instruction `0x3C2F` ko decode karo.
questions.explanation: Har hex digit 4 bits hai: 3 | C | 2F. Upar ka digit 3 = opcode, agla C = 12 = register, aur neeche ke do digits `0x2F` = 2·16 + 15 = 47 = immediate. Trap: immediate ko sirf aakhri digit F = 15 samajhna; ya fields ki order ulti kar dena; ya bytes (`0x3C` = 60) ko fields maan lena.

questions.question: Binary number 1011 0110 ko hex mein kya likhenge?
questions.explanation: Har 4 bits ek hex digit: 1011 = 11 = B, aur 0110 = 6. To 1011 0110 = `0xB6`. Trap: 0x6B, nibbles ki order ulti kar dena; 0xB5 ya 0xA6, ek nibble ka value galat ginna (0110 = 6, aur 1011 = B, A nahi).

questions.question: 8 bits ke unsigned number ki sabse badi value kya hai?
questions.explanation: n bits unsigned: 0 se 2ⁿ − 1. 8 bits: 2⁸ − 1 = 255 (1111 1111). Trap: 256, yeh total patterns ki ginti hai, par 0 bhi ek pattern hai; 127, yeh signed (two's complement) ki maximum value hai.

questions.question: ASCII maan kar, is statement ka output kya hoga?
questions.code: printf("%d\n", 'a' - 'A');
questions.explanation: `'a'` = 97 aur `'A'` = 65, to 97 − 65 = 32. Isi wajah se kisi bhi capital letter mein 32 jodne par uska small letter milta hai. Trap: 26, alphabet ke letters ki ginti se confuse hona; 0, sochna ki dono "same letter" hain.

questions.question: −37 ko 8-bit two's complement mein kaise likhenge?
questions.explanation: 37 = 32 + 4 + 1 = 0010 0101. Saare bits invert: 1101 1010. Phir +1: 1101 1011 = `0xDB`. Trap: 0xDA, sirf invert karke ruk jaana (one's complement); 0xA5, sign-magnitude (MSB 1 aur baaki 37); 0x25 to +37 hai.

questions.question: 8-bit two's complement hardware par 100 + 50 kiya gaya. Result ke 8-bit pattern ko signed number ki tarah padho to value kya hogi?
questions.explanation: 100 + 50 = 150 = 1001 0110. 8-bit signed range sirf −128 se 127 hai, aur is pattern ka MSB 1 hai, to yeh negative padha jaayega: 150 − 256 = −106. Trap: 150, overflow ko ignore karna; 127, sochna ki hardware value ko maximum par rok deta hai (bits bas wrap hote hain). (C mein signed overflow UB hai; yeh hardware ke bits ki baat hai.)

questions.question: Ek toy CPU ke 16-bit instruction mein upar ke 5 bits opcode, agle 3 bits register number, aur neeche ke 8 bits two's complement immediate hain. Instruction `0x2BF6` decode karo.
questions.explanation: Binary: 0010 1011 1111 0110. Upar ke 5 bits 00101 = 5 (opcode), agle 3 bits 011 = 3 (register), neeche ke 8 bits 1111 0110 = 246 unsigned. MSB 1 hai, to signed value 246 − 256 = −10 (ya invert + 1: 0000 1001 + 1 = 10). Trap: opcode 2, register 11, yaani fields ko hex digits ki seema par kaatna; 246, immediate ko unsigned padhna; −9, invert karke +1 bhool jaana.

questions.question: ASCII maan kar, is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
char c = 'd';
printf("%c %d %d\n", c - 'a' + 'A', c - 'a' + 1, c - 'a' + 'A');
questions.explanation: `'d'` = 100 aur `'a'` = 97, to `c - 'a'` = 3. Pehla: 3 + 65 = 68, jo `%c` mein 'D' hai. Doosra: 3 + 1 = 4 (d alphabet ka 4th letter). Teesra wahi 68 hai, par `%d` number dikhata hai. Trap: 3, `+ 1` bhool jaana; 100, sochna ki `%d` c ki original value dikhayega; "C 3 67", d ko alphabet ka 3rd letter maan lena (a se ginti 1 se hoti hai).

questions.question: 8-bit hardware par `0xF0 + 0x20` kiya. 8-bit result kya hai, aur agar dono inputs ko signed (two's complement) maano to yeh kaunsa addition hai?
questions.explanation: 0xF0 + 0x20 = 0x110, par 8 bits mein sirf neeche ke 8 bits bachte hain: 0x10 = 16 (carry gir jaata hai). Signed mein 0xF0 = 1111 0000 = 240 − 256 = −16, aur 0x20 = 32, to −16 + 32 = 16, jo result se match karta hai. Trap: 0x110 ko 9 bits ki jagah 8 mein maan lena; −112, 0xF0 ko sign-magnitude ki tarah padhna; −15, invert ke baad +1 bhool jaana (one's complement).

questions.question: Ek 32-bit instruction format mein 6-bit opcode, do 5-bit register fields, aur baaki bits ek two's complement immediate hain. Kitne alag opcodes, kitne registers ko naam diya ja sakta hai, aur immediate ki range kya hai?
questions.explanation: Opcode: 2⁶ = 64. Register field: 2⁵ = 32 registers. Immediate bits: 32 − 6 − 5 − 5 = 16, aur 16-bit two's complement range −2¹⁵ se 2¹⁵ − 1 = −32768 se 32767. Trap: 0 se 65535, immediate ko unsigned maanna; 6 aur 5, bits ki ginti ko hi values ki ginti samajhna; 32/64 ko aapas mein badal dena.

weeks.title: Variables, Types and Expressions
weeks.summary: Is week aap C program ka structure, variables aur data types, operators ki precedence, integer division aur type conversion seekhoge, taaki koi bhi expression ka result khud nikaal sako.
concepts: **Program structure**: upar `#include` lines, phir `main` function, uske andar declarations aur statements. Comments do tarah ke hote hain: `/* ... */` aur `// ...`. Compiler comments ko ignore karta hai.

**Variables aur types**: use karne se pehle variable declare karna padta hai, jaise `int count = 0;`. Typical 64-bit Linux gcc par sizes: `char` 1 byte, `int` 4, `float` 4, `double` 8. Local variable ko initialise na karo to usme garbage value hoti hai.

**Format specifiers**: `printf` mein `%d` (int), `%c` (char), `%f` (float/double), `%.2f` (2 decimal places). `scanf` ko variable ka address chahiye: `scanf("%d", &x);`, aur double padhne ke liye `%lf`.

**Integer division aur %**: dono operands int hon to result bhi int, decimal part kat jaata hai (zero ki taraf): `7 / 2` = 3, `-7 / 2` = −3. Remainder ka sign pehle operand jaisa: `7 % 3` = 1, `-7 % 3` = −1.

**Type conversion**: mixed expression mein chhota type bade mein badal jaata hai (int + double → double). Double ko int variable mein rakho to fraction kat jaata hai (`int k = 3.99;` → 3). Cast se zabardasti convert karo: `(double)a / b`.

**Precedence aur associativity**: `*`, `/`, `%` pehle; phir `+`, `-`; phir comparisons; sabse baad assignment. Same level ke operators left se right chalte hain, par assignment right se left. Shak ho to brackets lagao.

**Increment aur compound operators**: `x++` pehle purani value deta hai phir badhata hai, `++x` pehle badhata hai phir nayi value deta hai. `x += 3` matlab `x = x + 3`. Ek hi expression mein ek variable ko do baar badalna (jaise `i = i++;`) undefined behaviour hai.

example.problem: Teen marks 7, 8 aur 10 hain. Neeche ka code do averages print karta hai. Output kya hoga aur dono alag kyun hain?
steps: Sum = 7 + 8 + 10 = 25, jo ek int hai.
`avg1 = sum / 3`: dono int hain, isliye integer division: 25 / 3 = 8. Phir 8 float mein jaata hai: 8.00.
`avg2 = sum / 3.0`: 3.0 double hai, isliye sum bhi double ban jaata hai: 25 / 3.0 = 8.333...
`%.2f` do decimal places tak round karke dikhata hai: 8.33.
Answer: **8.00 8.33**. Fraction chahiye to kam se kam ek operand floating type ka hona chahiye.

mistakes: `float avg = sum / n;` likh kar sochna ki decimal aayega. Division pehle int mein ho chuka hota hai; `(float)sum / n` likho.
`scanf("%d", x);` likhna (`&` ke bina). `scanf` ko address chahiye, warna program crash kar sakta hai.
Precedence ka andaza lagana, jaise `a + b / 2` ko average samajhna. Yeh `a + (b / 2)` hai; `(a + b) / 2` likho.
revision: int / int = int (fraction kat jaata hai, zero ki taraf).
`%` ka sign pehle operand jaisa hota hai.
int + double → double; double → int assignment fraction kaat deta hai.
`*` `/` `%` pehle, `+` `-` baad mein; same level left se right.
`x++` purani value deta hai, `++x` nayi.

questions.question: Is statement ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Dono operands int hain, isliye `17 / 5` = 3 (3.4 ka fraction kat jaata hai), aur remainder `17 % 5` = 17 − 15 = 2. Trap: 3.4, normal division jaisa sochna; aur `%d` waise bhi decimal nahi dikhata.

questions.question: Is code ke baad x ki value kya hogi?
questions.explanation: `x += 3 * 2` ka matlab hai `x = x + (3 * 2)`. Right side pehle poori evaluate hoti hai: 6. Phir 10 + 6 = 16. Trap: 26, yeh sochna ki `x += 3` pehle hota hai aur phir result ×2 (`(10 + 3) * 2`).

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?

weeks.title: Decisions and Loops
weeks.summary: Is week aap `if`/`else if`, `switch` (fall-through ke saath), `for`, `while`, `do-while` loops aur `break`/`continue` se program ka flow control karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Condition ka matlab**: C mein koi bhi non-zero value true hai aur 0 false. Comparison (`x > 3`) true par 1 aur false par 0 deta hai.
**if / else if / else**: upar se neeche conditions check hoti hain, aur pehli true condition ka block chalta hai, baaki skip. Ek se zyada statement ho to braces `{ }` lagao.
**Dangling else**: `else` hamesha sabse paas wale bina-else `if` ke saath judta hai, indentation chahe kuch bhi dikhaye. Braces lagakar intent saaf karo.
**= vs ==**: `if (x = 0)` comparison nahi, assignment hai. x 0 ban jaata hai aur condition false. Compare karne ke liye `==` likho (gcc `-Wall` iski warning deta hai).

**switch aur fall-through**: `switch` integer ya char value ko `case` labels se milata hai. Match hone ke baad `break` tak saare neeche ke cases chalte rehte hain (fall-through). Koi match na ho to `default` chalta hai.

**for, while, do-while**: `for (init; condition; update)` gin kar chalne wale loops ke liye. `while` pehle condition check karta hai, isliye 0 baar bhi chal sakta hai. `do { } while (cond);` body pehle chalata hai, isliye kam se kam ek baar zaroor chalta hai.

**break aur continue**: `break` sabse andar wale loop (ya switch) se bahar nikalta hai. `continue` is round ka baaki hissa chhod kar agle round par jaata hai; `for` mein continue ke baad bhi update (`i++`) chalta hai.
**Short-circuit**: `a && b` mein a false ho to b evaluate hi nahi hota; `a || b` mein a true ho to b skip. Isliye `if (n != 0 && x / n > 2)` safe hai.

example.problem: `while` loop se 1234 ke digits ulte karke number banao.

Round 4: digit = 1, rev = 4321, n = 0. Ab `n > 0` false, loop khatam.
Answer: **4321**. Yahan loop kitni baar chalega pehle se pata nahi tha, isliye `while` sahi choice hai.

mistakes: `switch` ke case mein `break` bhool jaana. Neeche ke cases bhi chal jaate hain. Har case ke end mein `break` lagao, jab tak fall-through jaan-boojh kar na ho.
`for (i = 0; i < n; i++);` — loop ke baad semicolon. Loop khaali chalta hai aur neeche ka block sirf ek baar. Semicolon hatao.
Loop ki ginti mein off-by-one: `i <= n` aur `i < n` mein ek round ka farq hai. Pehli aur aakhri value ko haath se check karo.
revision: Non-zero = true, 0 = false.
`else` sabse paas wale `if` ka hota hai.
`switch` mein `break` ke bina fall-through hota hai.
`do-while` kam se kam ek baar chalta hai.
`break` loop se bahar; `continue` agle round par (for mein update chalta hai).

weeks.title: Functions, Scope and Recursion
weeks.summary: Is week aap functions declare aur define karna, call by value, runtime stack, recursion, aur variables ka scope aur lifetime (local, global, static) seekhoge.
concepts: **Functions kyun**: bada problem chhote, test karne laayak tukdon mein toot jaata hai, aur ek hi code baar-baar likhna nahi padta. Function ka ek return type, naam, parameters aur body hoti hai.

**Declaration vs definition**: prototype (`int square(int x);`) compiler ko function ka naam, return type aur parameter types batata hai, aur `main` se pehle likha jaata hai. Definition mein poori body hoti hai. Function ko use karne se pehle uska declaration dikhna chahiye.

**Call by value**: C arguments ki **copy** function ko deta hai. Function ke andar parameter badlo to caller ka variable nahi badalta. Isliye simple `swap(int a, int b)` kaam nahi karta (iska hal pointers hain, agle week).

**Runtime stack**: har function call ke liye stack par ek **frame** banta hai jisme parameters, local variables aur return address hote hain. Function return hote hi frame hat jaata hai, aur uske locals khatam.

**Recursion**: function khud ko call karta hai. Do cheezein zaroori: **base case** (jahan recursion ruke) aur aisa recursive case jo base ki taraf badhe. Har call ka apna frame hota hai; base case na ho to stack overflow hota hai.

**Scope**: variable kahan dikhta hai. Block ke andar declared variable sirf us block mein. Andar same naam ka variable bahar wale ko **shadow** (chhupa) deta hai. Global variable (sab functions ke bahar) har function mein dikhta hai.

**Lifetime aur static**: normal local (automatic) variable har call par naya banta hai. `static` local sirf ek baar initialise hota hai aur calls ke beech apni value yaad rakhta hai. Globals aur statics program ke poore time tak zinda rehte hain, aur by default 0 se initialise hote hain.

Upar naye frames: `fact(3)` → `3 * fact(2)`, `fact(2)` → `2 * fact(1)`.
`fact(1)` base case hai, 1 return karta hai, aur uska frame hat jaata hai.
Sabse zyada 4 frames ek saath stack par the (plus `main` ka).
Answer: **24**.

mistakes: Function ko call karne ke baad define karna aur upar prototype na dena. Purane compilers galat type maan lete hain; aaj ka gcc warning/error deta hai. `main` se pehle prototype likho.
Recursion mein base case bhool jaana ya galat likhna (jaise `n == 0` par ruko jab n kabhi 0 nahi banta). Infinite recursion → stack overflow.
Sochna ki function ke andar parameter badalne se caller ka variable badal jaayega. Call by value mein sirf copy badalti hai.
revision: Prototype: return type, naam, parameter types, end mein `;`.
C hamesha call by value hai; copy jaati hai.
Har call = naya stack frame; return par frame hat jaata hai.
Recursion = base case + chhota hota hua recursive case.
`static` local ek baar initialise hota hai aur value yaad rakhta hai.

weeks.title: Pointers and Memory Layout
weeks.summary: Is week aap pointers (`&` aur `*`), pointers se function mein variables badalna, `sizeof`, endianness, alignment, aur compiler optimisation ki ek jhalak seekhoge.
concepts: **Address-of aur dereference**: `&x` variable x ka memory address deta hai. Pointer variable address rakhta hai: `int *p = &x;`. `*p` us address par rakhi value hai, isliye `*p = 5;` asal mein x ko 5 bana deta hai.

**Pointer type**: `int *` int ko point karta hai, `char *` char ko. Type batata hai ki `*p` karne par kitni bytes aur kis tarah padhni hain. Address print karne ke liye `%p`, aur "kahin point nahi karta" ke liye `NULL`.

**Pointers aur functions**: C call by value hai, par agar address (copy) bhejo to function us address par likh kar caller ka variable badal sakta hai: `swap(&x, &y)` jismein `void swap(int *a, int *b)`. `scanf` isi wajah se `&` maangta hai.

**sizeof**: compile time par bytes batata hai, type `size_t` (print ke liye `%zu`). Typical 64-bit Linux gcc: `char` 1, `int` 4, `double` 8, aur **har** pointer 8 bytes, chahe woh kisi bhi type ko point kare.

**Endianness**: multi-byte value ki bytes memory mein kis order mein hain. **Little-endian** (x86, most ARM) mein sabse kam significant byte sabse chhote address par: `0x12345678` memory mein 78 56 34 12. Big-endian mein ulta.

**Alignment**: CPU ko pasand hai ki 4-byte int aise address par ho jo 4 ka multiple ho, aur 8-byte double 8 ke multiple par. Isse access tez hota hai. Isi wajah se structs mein padding aati hai (week 8).

**Compiler optimisation ki jhalak**: `-O2` par compiler variables ko registers mein rakh sakta hai, constant expressions pehle hi compute kar sakta hai (`3 * 4` → 12), aur jo result kabhi use nahi hota uska code hata sakta hai. Jis variable ka address liya gaya ho use aam taur par memory mein rehna padta hai. `volatile` compiler ko batata hai ki is variable ke reads/writes optimise mat karo (hardware registers ke liye).

Function return hota hai; a, b, t khatam, par x aur y ki memory badal chuki hai.
Answer: **7 3** print hota hai.

mistakes: Uninitialised pointer par likhna: `int *p; *p = 5;`. p kisi random address ko point karta hai, crash ya memory corruption. Pehle `p = &x;` (ya valid memory) do.
`int *p, q;` se sochna ki dono pointer hain. Sirf p pointer hai, q ek int hai. Har pointer ke saath `*` lagao: `int *p, *q;`.
`sizeof(p)` (pointer ka size, 8) aur `sizeof(*p)` (jis cheez ko point karta hai uska size) mein confuse hona.
revision: `&x` = address, `*p` = us address ki value.
Function mein variable badalna ho to uska address bhejo.
64-bit par har pointer 8 bytes; `sizeof` ke liye `%zu`.
Little-endian: lowest byte lowest address par.
Alignment: int 4 ke multiple par, double 8 ke multiple par.

weeks.title: Arrays, Pointer Arithmetic and Strings
weeks.summary: Is week aap arrays, pointer arithmetic, arrays aur pointers ka farq, `'\0'` par khatam hone wali strings, aur `string.h` ke functions (`strlen`, `strcpy`, `strcat`, `strcmp`) seekhoge.
concepts: **Array**: ek hi type ke elements memory mein lagataar. `int a[5];` ke index 0 se 4 tak. C bounds check nahi karta, `a[5]` likhna array ke bahar padhna hai (undefined behaviour).
**Array name aur pointer**: zyada tar expressions mein array ka naam pehle element ke pointer mein badal jaata hai (decay): `a` ≡ `&a[0]`. Aur `a[i]` ka asli matlab hai `*(a + i)`.

**Pointer arithmetic**: `p + 1` agle **element** par jaata hai, agle byte par nahi; address `sizeof(*p)` bytes badhta hai (int ke liye 4). Ek hi array ke do pointers ka farq (`q - p`) elements ki ginti deta hai.

**Array vs pointer**: `sizeof(a)` poore array ki bytes deta hai (`int a[10]` → 40), par pointer ka `sizeof` 8 hai. Array naam ko reassign nahi kar sakte (`a = b;` error). Function ko array do to asal mein pointer jaata hai, isliye andar size pata nahi chalta; size alag parameter mein bhejo.

**Strings**: C mein string ek `char` array hai jiske end mein `'\0'` (null character, value 0) hota hai. `"hi"` 3 bytes leta hai: h, i, `'\0'`. `%s` aur string functions `'\0'` milne tak hi chalte hain.
**char array vs string literal**: `char s[] = "hi";` apni copy banata hai jise badal sakte ho. `char *s = "hi";` ek read-only literal ko point karta hai; `s[0] = 'H';` undefined behaviour hai.

**string.h**: `strlen(s)` `'\0'` se pehle tak ke characters ginta hai. `strcpy(d, s)` copy, `strcat(d, s)` end mein jodta hai (d mein jagah honi chahiye). `strcmp(a, b)` pehle alag character par compare karke negative, 0 ya positive deta hai. Strings ko `==` se compare mat karo, woh addresses compare karta hai.

mistakes: String ke liye jagah ginte waqt `'\0'` bhool jaana: "hello" ke liye `char s[5]` kam hai, `char s[6]` chahiye.
`if (s1 == s2)` se strings compare karna. Yeh addresses compare karta hai; `strcmp(s1, s2) == 0` use karo.
Function ke andar `sizeof(arr) / sizeof(arr[0])` se length nikalna. Wahan arr pointer hai, isliye galat answer aata hai; length parameter bhejo.
revision: `a[i]` = `*(a + i)`; `p + 1` ek element aage.
`sizeof` array par poori size, pointer par 8.
String = chars + `'\0'`; `strlen` `'\0'` nahi ginta.
`strcmp`: 0 matlab barabar.
Function ko array dena = pointer dena.

weeks.title: Structures, Unions and Enums
weeks.summary: Is week aap `struct` se alag-alag types ko ek saath rakhna, `typedef`, `union`, `enum`, aur structs ki size, padding aur alignment ko intro level par seekhoge.
concepts: **struct**: alag types ke members ko ek naam ke neeche jodta hai: `struct point { int x; int y; };`. Member tak `.` se pahunchte hain (`p.x`). Pointer ho to `->`: `ptr->x` ≡ `(*ptr).x`.
**typedef**: kisi type ko naya naam deta hai, jaise `typedef struct { ... } Student;`. Uske baad seedha `Student s;` likh sakte ho, har baar `struct` likhne ki zaroorat nahi.

**Struct copy**: `b = a;` saare members copy karta hai (andar ke arrays bhi). Struct ko function mein by value bhejo to poori copy jaati hai; asli struct badalna ho ya badi copy se bachna ho to pointer bhejo.

**Padding aur alignment**: har member apne alignment ke multiple wale offset par rakha jaata hai (typical 64-bit gcc: char 1, int 4, double 8). Beech mein khaali bytes (padding) aa sakti hain, aur poore struct ki size sabse bade alignment ki multiple tak round hoti hai.
**Member order**: bade members pehle rakhne se padding kam hoti hai. `{char; int; char;}` 12 bytes leta hai, par `{int; char; char;}` sirf 8.

**union**: saare members **ek hi memory** share karte hain; size sabse bade member jitni (alignment tak round). Ek member mein likhne se baaki ki bytes bhi badal jaati hain, isliye ek time par ek hi member ka matlab hota hai.
**enum**: naam wale integer constants. Pehla 0 se shuru, har agla pichhle + 1, jab tak tum khud value na do: `enum { MON = 1, TUE, WED };` mein TUE = 2, WED = 3.

Order badal kar `{ double b; int c; char a; }` karo to 8 + 4 + 1 = 13 → round karke 16.
Answer: **24 bytes** (reorder karne par 16).

mistakes: Struct ki size ko members ki sizes ka seedha jod samajhna (1 + 8 + 4 = 13). Padding ki wajah se asli size zyada hoti hai; hamesha `sizeof` use karo.
Pointer ke saath `.` lagana (`ptr.x`). Pointer se member ke liye `ptr->x` chahiye.
Union ke ek member mein likh kar doosre se "alag" value ki ummeed karna. Sab ek hi bytes hain.
revision: `.` struct ke saath, `->` struct pointer ke saath.
Struct assignment = poori copy.
Size = members + padding, sabse bade alignment ka multiple.
Union size = sabse bada member; memory shared.
enum: 0 se shuru, har agla +1, jab tak value na di jaaye.

weeks.title: Dynamic Memory: Stack and Heap
weeks.summary: Is week aap stack aur heap ka farq, `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free`, memory leaks aur dangling pointers, aur 2-D arrays (static aur dynamic) seekhoge.
concepts: **Stack vs heap**: local variables function ke stack frame mein rehte hain aur return par apne aap khatam. **Heap** se memory tab maangte hain jab size runtime par pata chale ya data ko function ke baad bhi zinda rehna ho; yeh tab tak rehti hai jab tak tum `free` na karo.

**malloc**: `malloc(n)` n bytes deta hai aur `void *` return karta hai; memory uninitialised (garbage) hoti hai. Hamesha bytes mein socho: `malloc(n * sizeof(int))`. Memory na mile to `NULL` aata hai, isliye check karo. `<stdlib.h>` include karo.
**calloc**: `calloc(count, size)` count elements ki jagah deta hai aur saari bytes 0 kar deta hai.

**realloc**: `realloc(p, newsize)` block ko bada/chhota karta hai. Purana data (dono sizes mein jo chhota ho utna) bacha rehta hai, par block naye address par move ho sakta hai. Result pehle temporary pointer mein lo; fail hone par `NULL` aata hai aur purana block abhi bhi valid hota hai.

**free aur dangling pointer**: `free(p)` block heap ko wapas deta hai, par p mein purana address reh jaata hai (dangling). Use use karna ya dobara free karna undefined behaviour hai. Free ke baad `p = NULL;` achhi aadat hai.

**Memory leak**: heap block ka aakhri pointer kho diya (overwrite ya function khatam) bina `free` kiye, to woh memory program khatam hone tak waste. Function se local variable ka address return karna bhi galat hai, kyunki frame hat chuka hota hai.

**2-D arrays**: `int m[3][4];` memory mein row-major hai: pehle poori row 0, phir row 1. `m[i][j]` start se `i·4 + j` elements door hai. Dynamic 2-D ke do tareeke: ek bada block aur index `i * cols + j`, ya rows ke pointers ka array (`int **`) jisme har row alag `malloc`.

example.problem: User se n = 4 milta hai. Heap par n ints ka array banao, usme i² (i = 1 se 4) bharo, sum nikaalo aur memory free karo.
steps: `int *a = malloc(n * sizeof(int));`: 4 · 4 = 16 bytes.
`if (a == NULL)` par error dikha kar ruko.
`free(a); a = NULL;`: memory wapas, aur dangling pointer nahi bacha.
Answer: **30**.

mistakes: `malloc(10)` likh kar 10 ints ki ummeed karna. Yeh 10 **bytes** hain; `malloc(10 * sizeof(int))` likho.
`p = realloc(p, size);` likhna. Fail hone par p `NULL` ho jaata hai aur purana block leak. Pehle temporary pointer mein lo.
`free` ke baad pointer use karna ya do baar `free` karna. Free ke turant baad pointer ko `NULL` kar do.
revision: Stack: automatic, function ke saath khatam. Heap: `free` tak.
`malloc` garbage deta hai, `calloc` zero.
`realloc` data bachata hai par address badal sakta hai.
Leak = pointer kho gaya, free nahi hua. Dangling = free ho gaya, pointer bacha.
`m[i][j]` offset = `i * cols + j` elements (row-major).

weeks.title: File Handling and Bit Manipulation
weeks.summary: Is week aap text aur binary files ke saath kaam karna (`fopen`, `fprintf`, `fscanf`, `fgets`, `fread`, `fwrite`, `fclose`) aur bitwise operators, shifts aur masks se bits ko set, clear, toggle aur test karna seekhoge.
concepts: **FILE * aur fopen**: `FILE *fp = fopen("data.txt", "r");`. Modes: `"r"` padhna (file honi chahiye), `"w"` likhna (nayi banti hai, purani ho to khaali ho jaati hai), `"a"` end mein jodna; binary ke liye `"rb"`, `"wb"`. File na khule to `NULL` milta hai, hamesha check karo. Kaam ke baad `fclose(fp)`, jo buffer ko bhi flush karta hai.

**Text I/O**: `fprintf(fp, ...)` aur `fscanf(fp, ...)` printf/scanf jaise hi hain, bas file ke saath. `fscanf` kitne items match hue woh return karta hai, aur file khatam hone par `EOF`. `fgets(buf, n, fp)` ek line padhta hai, zyada se zyada n − 1 characters, newline ko bhi rakhta hai, aur end mein `'\0'` lagata hai.

**Binary I/O**: `fwrite(ptr, size, count, fp)` memory ki bytes jaisi hain waisi likhta hai; 10 ints = 40 bytes (int 4 bytes). `fread` same arguments leta hai aur **kitne items** pure padhe woh return karta hai, jo file khatam hone par count se kam ho sakta hai.
**Bitwise operators**: `&` (dono 1 to 1), `|` (koi ek 1 to 1), `^` (alag hon to 1), `~` (har bit ulta). Yeh har bit par alag kaam karte hain; `&&`, `||` jaise logical operators se confuse mat karo.

**Shifts**: `x << k` bits ko left khiskata hai, yaani 2ᵏ se guna (agar overflow na ho). Unsigned `x >> k` right khiskata hai, yaani 2ᵏ se integer division. Bit manipulation ke liye unsigned types use karo; negative numbers ko shift karna implementation-defined/undefined ho sakta hai.
**Masks**: bit k ke liye mask `1u << k`. Set: `x | (1u << k)`. Clear: `x & ~(1u << k)`. Toggle: `x ^ (1u << k)`. Test: `(x >> k) & 1`.
**Useful tricks**: `x & (x - 1)` sabse neeche wala 1-bit hata deta hai, `x & (~x + 1)` sirf sabse neeche wala 1-bit bachata hai, aur `a ^ a` = 0.

example.problem: 45 ke binary mein kitne 1-bits hain? Shift aur mask wale loop se gino.
steps: Har round mein `x & 1` sabse neeche ka bit deta hai, phir `x >>= 1` use hata deta hai.
x 0 hote hi loop rukta hai (6 rounds).
Answer: **4** set bits.

mistakes: `fopen` ka result check na karna. File na mili to fp `NULL` hai aur agla `fprintf`/`fgets` crash karega.
Bit test ke liye `if (x & 1 << k == 0)` likhna. `==` ki precedence `&` se zyada hai; brackets lagao: `if ((x & (1u << k)) == 0)`.
`&` aur `&&` mein confuse hona: `6 & 1` = 0 hai, par `6 && 1` = 1.
revision: `"w"` purani file khaali kar deta hai, `"a"` end mein jodta hai.
`fgets` newline rakhta hai; `fread` items ki ginti return karta hai.
Set: `|`, clear: `& ~`, toggle: `^`, test: `>> k & 1`.
`x << k` = ×2ᵏ, unsigned `x >> k` = ÷2ᵏ.
`x & (x - 1)` lowest set bit hata deta hai.

questions.question: File ki pehli line "network" hai (uske baad newline). fp sahi se khula hai aur string.h included hai. Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `fgets(buf, 6, fp)` zyada se zyada 6 − 1 = 5 characters padhta hai aur end mein `'\0'` lagata hai, taaki buf ke 6 bytes mein fit ho. To buf = "netwo", length 5. Newline tak pahunche hi nahi. Trap: 6 characters, `'\0'` ki jagah bhool jaana; poori line, sochna ki `fgets` hamesha newline tak padhta hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 0010 1100 mein right se bits: bit 0 = 0, bit 1 = 0, bit 2 = 1, bit 3 = 1, bit 4 = 0, bit 5 = 1. To a = 1, b = 0. `& ~(1u << 5)` bit 5 clear karta hai: 0000 1100 = 0xC. Trap: bits ko left se ginna (tab a = 0, b = 1 lagta); 2C, clear ke baad bhi purani value maanna.

questions.question: File "nums.txt" mein bas yeh text hai: `4 7 x 9`. fp use padhne ke liye sahi se khula hai. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `fscanf` kitne items match hue woh return karta hai. 4 aur 7 par 1 milta hai. "x" `%d` se match nahi hota, to 0 return hota hai (EOF nahi) aur `== 1` false: loop ruk jaata hai. sum = 11, n = 2. Trap: "20 3", sochna ki fscanf "x" ko skip karke 9 padh lega; infinite loop, yeh tab hota jab condition `!= EOF` hoti, kyunki 0 baar-baar aata.

questions.question: Int 4 bytes, aur maan lo dono `fopen` safal hain. Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `fwrite` aur `fread` **items** ginte hain, bytes nahi: w = 5. Pehla `fread` 3 ints (1, 2, 3) padhta hai: r1 = 3. File mein sirf 2 ints bache hain, to doosra `fread` 2 deta hai aur b[0], b[1] mein 4, 5 likhta hai: b[0] = 4. Trap: 20/12/8, bytes ginna; "0" aur b[0] = 1, sochna ki doosra fread kuch nahi padhega ya b nahi badlega.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `x >> 2` = 0011 0101, aur `& 0x7` neeche ke 3 bits rakhta hai: 101 = 5 (yaani bits 2–4). `x >> 5` = 110 = 6. `x & 0xF` = 7, `<< 4` se 0x70; `x >> 4` = 0xD; OR karke 0x7D (dono nibbles badal gaye). Trap: D7, swap ko ignore karna; 2, 3 jagah shift kar dena; 13, `x >> 4` ko top samajhna.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `x & (x - 1)` sabse neeche ka 1-bit hatata hai; result 0 tabhi hai jab sirf ek hi bit 1 ho, yaani 2 ki power. 16 (10000) haan, 24 (11000) nahi, 1 haan; 0 ko `v[i] != 0` pehle hi rok deta hai. c = 2. `x & (~x + 1)` sirf sabse neeche ka 1-bit rakhta hai: 24 = 11000 → 01000 = 8. Trap: 3, 0 ko bhi ginna; 1, 1 ko 2 ki power na maanna (2⁰ = 1); 16, sabse upar wala bit le lena.

weeks.title: Preprocessor, Headers and the Build Pipeline
weeks.summary: Is week aap `#define` macros aur unke traps, `#include`, include guards, conditional compilation, multi-file projects aur header files, aur preprocess → compile → assemble → link stages seekhoge.
concepts: **Preprocessor**: compiler se pehle chalta hai aur `#` se shuru hone wali lines ko sambhalta hai. Yeh sirf **text replace** karta hai; C ke types ya precedence ko nahi samajhta.

**#define aur macros**: `#define PI 3.14159` ek constant hai. Function-like macro: `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))`. Har parameter aur poore macro ko brackets mein rakho, warna `SQ(1 + 2)` jaisi cheez galat expand hoti hai. Argument jo do baar use ho (jaise `SQ(i++)`) side effect do baar karta hai.
**#include**: `#include <stdio.h>` system directories mein dhoondhta hai, `#include "myfile.h"` pehle current project folder mein. Preprocessor us file ka poora text wahin chipka deta hai.

**Include guards**: header do baar include ho jaaye (seedha ya kisi doosre header ke through) to struct jaisi definitions do baar aa jaati hain aur compile error aata hai. Hal: `#ifndef POINT_H` / `#define POINT_H` / ... / `#endif` (ya `#pragma once`).

**Conditional compilation**: `#if`, `#elif`, `#else`, `#endif`, `#ifdef NAME`, `#ifndef NAME`. Jo hissa condition mein false hai woh compiler tak pahunchta hi nahi. `gcc -DDEBUG prog.c` se command line par DEBUG define kar sakte ho.

**Multi-file projects**: header (`.h`) mein declarations: prototypes, `extern int count;`, struct types. Ek `.c` file mein definition: `int count = 0;`. File level par `static` variable/function sirf usi file mein dikhta hai. Har `.c` alag compile hoti hai (translation unit).

**Build stages**: preprocess (`gcc -E`, output `.i`) → compile to assembly (`gcc -S`, `.s`) → assemble to object code (`gcc -c`, `.o`) → link (sab `.o` aur libraries jod kar executable). "undefined reference" ek **linker** error hai: declaration mil gaya par definition kahin nahi mili.

example.problem: `#define DOUBLE(x) x + x` hai. `3 * DOUBLE(2)` ki value kya hogi, aur sahi macro kya hona chahiye?
steps: Preprocessor sirf text badalta hai: `3 * DOUBLE(2)` → `3 * 2 + 2`.
Ab normal precedence: `3 * 2` = 6, phir 6 + 2 = 8.
Hum 3 · (2 + 2) = 12 chahte the.
Sahi macro: `#define DOUBLE(x) ((x) + (x))`. Ab `3 * ((2) + (2))` = 12.
Answer: buggy macro se **8**, brackets wale macro se **12**.

mistakes: Macro mein brackets na lagana. Har parameter ko `(x)` aur poori body ko bahar ke brackets mein rakho.
Header mein variable ki definition (`int count = 0;`) likhna. Do `.c` files include karengi to linker "multiple definition" dega. Header mein `extern int count;`, aur definition ek hi `.c` mein.
`#define N 10;` (end mein semicolon). `int a[N];` ban jaata hai `int a[10;];` aur ajeeb error aata hai. `#define` ke end mein `;` mat lagao.
revision: Preprocessor = text replacement, compile se pehle.
Macro: har parameter aur poori body brackets mein.
Include guard: `#ifndef` / `#define` / `#endif`.
Header mein declarations (`extern`), `.c` mein definitions.
Stages: `-E` preprocess, `-S` assembly, `-c` object, phir link.
"undefined reference" = linker error.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
#define SQ(x) x * x
printf("%d\n", SQ(2 + 3));
questions.explanation: Preprocessor bina brackets ke text badalta hai: `SQ(2 + 3)` → `2 + 3 * 2 + 3`. Precedence se `3 * 2` = 6 pehle, phir 2 + 6 + 3 = 11. Trap: 25, macro ko function ki tarah samajhna jo pehle `2 + 3` = 5 karta. Isliye `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))` likhte hain.

questions.question: Build ke kis stage par `undefined reference to 'compute'` jaisa error aata hai?
questions.explanation: Compiler ko sirf prototype chahiye, isliye woh call ko theek maan leta hai. Linker sab object files ko jodte waqt `compute` ki asli definition dhoondhta hai; na mile (jaise woh `.c` file build mein di hi nahi) to "undefined reference". Trap: compiler, par compiler ka error hota "implicit declaration" ya syntax error, undefined reference nahi.

questions.question: Yeh program `gcc prog.c` se (koi `-D` option nahi) compile karke chalaya. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `LEVEL` 2 hai, to `#if LEVEL > 1` true: "A" wali line rehti hai, aur `#elif` wala hissa hata diya jaata hai (if/elif mein ek hi chunta hai). DEBUG kahin define nahi hua, to `#else` wala "D". Output "AD". Trap: "ABD", yeh sochna ki `#elif` bhi true hai to woh bhi aayega; preprocessor bhi if-else-if ki tarah pehli true branch hi rakhta hai.

questions.question: `point.h` mein `struct point { int x, y; };` hai aur koi include guard nahi hai. `shapes.h` bhi `point.h` include karta hai. `main.c` dono ko include karta hai. `main.c` compile karne par kya hoga?
options: Compile error: struct point ek hi file mein do baar define hua
Theek chalega; preprocessor duplicate includes apne aap hata deta hai
questions.explanation: Preprocessor `point.h` ka text do baar main.c mein chipka deta hai, to ek hi translation unit mein `struct point` ki do definitions ho jaati hain: compile error ("redefinition"). Yeh linker tak pahunchta hi nahi. Hal: include guard (`#ifndef POINT_H` ...). Trap: "preprocessor apne aap hata deta hai", jo guard ke bina nahi hota.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Expand karo: `((i++) > (j) ? (i++) : (j))`. Pehla `i++` 5 deta hai, 5 > 3 true, aur i = 6. `?:` ke pehle operand ke baad sequence point hai, isliye yeh defined hai. Ab chuna gaya `(i++)` phir chalta hai: 6 deta hai aur i = 7. To m = 6, i = 7. Trap: "5 6", MAX ko function samajhna jisme `i++` ek hi baar chalta.

questions.question: Do files ko `gcc main.c a.c -o app` se build karke chalaya. Output kya hoga, aur agar `main.c` mein `extern int hidden;` likh kar `hidden` print karne ki koshish karein to kya hoga?
options: 12; hidden use karne par linker error (undefined reference), kyunki static use a.c tak seemit rakhta hai
10; kyunki extern count ki alag copy banata hai
Compile error: count do baar declare hua hai
questions.explanation: `extern int count;` sirf batata hai ki count kahin aur defined hai; linker use a.c wale count se jodta hai. Do baar `inc()` se count 10 → 12. `hidden` file-level `static` hai, iska naam a.c ke bahar dikhta hi nahi; main.c mein extern likh kar use karoge to linker ko koi bahar dikhne wala hidden nahi milega: undefined reference. Trap: "7 aayega", static ko normal global samajhna; "10", extern ko copy samajhna.

questions.question: `gcc -E prog.c` kya karta hai?
options: Sirf linking karke executable banata hai
questions.explanation: `-E` build ko preprocessing ke baad rok deta hai: includes chipak jaate hain, macros expand ho jaate hain, aur jo text bachta hai woh dikhta hai (`.i`). Trap: `-S` assembly deta hai aur `-c` object file; linking bina in options ke chalne wala aakhri stage hai.

questions.question: `#include "myfile.h"` (quotes wala) file ko sabse pehle kahan dhoondhta hai?
options: Sirf system ki include directories mein
Sirf compiler ke install folder mein
questions.explanation: Quotes wala include pehle current project folder (jahan source file hai) mein dekhta hai, phir system directories mein. `<...>` wala seedha system directories mein dhoondhta hai. Trap: dono ko same samajhna; isliye apni headers ke liye quotes aur standard headers ke liye `<...>` likhte hain.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Preprocessor text replace karta hai: `TOTAL + 1` → `N * 5 + 1` → `4 * 5 + 1`. `*` pehle: 20 + 1 = 21. Trap: 24, sochna ki TOTAL ek bracketed value hai, yaani `4 * (5 + 1)`; 25, macro ko "5" samajhna. Ek macro ke andar doosra macro use karna valid hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
#define HALF(x) x / 2
printf("%d\n", HALF(10 + 6));
questions.explanation: Expansion: `10 + 6 / 2`. Brackets nahi hain, to `/` pehle: 6 / 2 = 3, phir 10 + 3 = 13. Trap: 8, yeh maan lena ki macro function ki tarah pehle 16 nikaal kar aadha karega. Sahi macro: `#define HALF(x) ((x) / 2)`.

questions.question: Yeh program `gcc -DLIMIT=8 prog.c` se compile karke chalaya. Output kya hoga?
options: Compile error: LIMIT do baar define hua
questions.explanation: `-DLIMIT=8` command line par hi LIMIT ko 8 define kar deta hai. Isliye `#ifndef LIMIT` false hai aur file wala `#define LIMIT 5` compiler tak pahunchta hi nahi. 8 × 2 = 16. Trap: 10, file ki default value maan lena; compile error, yeh bhool jaana ki `#ifndef` isi ke liye laga hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: SQ theek likha hai, par CUBE mein aakhri x bina brackets ke hai. Expansion: `(((a + 1) * (a + 1)) * a + 1)`. Pehle 3 × 3 = 9, phir `9 * a` = 18 (kyunki `*` `+` se pehle), phir + 1 = 19. Trap: 27, sochna ki macro (a + 1) ko teeno jagah bracket karega; 18, aakhri + 1 bhool jaana; 9, sirf SQ ka hissa.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Pehla expansion: `((x++) < (y) ? (x++) : (y))`. Condition mein x++ 4 deta hai (4 < 6 true) aur x = 5. True branch mein phir `x++`: m = 5, x = 6. Doosra: `((y) < (x) ? (y) : (x))`, 6 < 6 false, to n = x = 6. Trap: "4 5 5", MIN ko function samajhna jisme x++ ek hi baar chalta; "5 5 6", n nikaalte waqt purana x (5) lena.

questions.question: `main.c` mein `int helper(void);` prototype hai aur `main` use call karta hai, par `helper` ki definition kisi bhi file mein nahi hai. Build: pehle `gcc -c main.c a.c`, phir `gcc main.o a.o -o app`. Kya hoga?
options: Compile theek hoga; linking par `undefined reference` aayega
`gcc -c main.c` par hi error aayega, kyunki helper ki body nahi mili
Preprocessor error aayega, kyunki helper ka header nahi mila
Program ban jaayega, aur helper call hone par runtime par crash hoga
questions.explanation: Compiler ko sirf declaration (prototype) chahiye taaki call check kar sake, to `gcc -c` dono files ke `.o` bana deta hai. Linker sab `.o` jodte waqt helper ki definition dhoondhta hai, nahi milti, to "undefined reference" linker error. Executable banta hi nahi, isliye runtime crash ka sawaal nahi. Trap: sochna ki compiler ko har function ki body usi file mein chahiye.

questions.question: `config.h` mein include guard hai, aur guard ke andar `int limit = 10;` likha hai. `a.c` aur `main.c` dono `config.h` include karte hain. `gcc a.c main.c -o app` se build karne par kya hoga?
options: Compile error: main.c mein limit do baar define hua
Theek chalega, kyunki include guard duplicate hata deta hai
Linker error: limit ki multiple definition
Theek chalega, har file ki apni alag limit hogi
questions.explanation: Include guard sirf ek hi `.c` file (translation unit) ke andar dobara include hone se bachata hai. a.c aur main.c alag-alag compile hote hain, to dono ke `.o` mein `limit` ki apni definition aa jaati hai. Linker dono ko jodte waqt "multiple definition" deta hai. Hal: header mein `extern int limit;` aur definition sirf ek `.c` mein. Trap: guard ko poore project ke liye samajhna; "alag limit", yeh sirf `static` se hota.

weeks.title: Revision: Tracing, Bugs and Debugging Habits
weeks.summary: Is week aap poore course ko jod kar revise karoge: programs ko trace table se trace karna, aam C bugs pehchanna, undefined behaviour se bachna, aur debugging ki achhi aadatein.
concepts: **Trace table**: har variable ka ek column banao aur har line ke baad nayi value likho. Loop mein har round ki ek row. Dimaag mein trace karne se zyada galti hoti hai, kaagaz par kam.

**Off-by-one errors**: n elements ke array ke index 0 se n − 1 hain, to loop `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)`. `i <= n` ek round zyada chalta hai aur array ke bahar padhta hai. Pehli aur aakhri iteration hamesha haath se check karo.
**Aam bugs ki list**: `=` ki jagah `==`, switch mein `break` missing, integer division (`1 / 2` = 0), uninitialised variable, `scanf` mein `&` missing, aur `if`/`for` ke baad galti se `;`.

**Memory bugs**: array ke bahar padhna/likhna, string mein `'\0'` ki jagah na rakhna, free ke baad pointer use karna (dangling), `free` bhool jaana (leak), aur local ka address return karna. Yeh aksar "kabhi chalta hai, kabhi nahi" wale bugs hote hain.

**Undefined behaviour (UB)**: jaise signed int overflow, `i = i++;`, uninitialised value padhna, ya array ke bahar jaana. C standard koi result guarantee nahi karta; output compiler aur optimisation ke saath badal sakta hai. Aise code ka "output" predict mat karo, use theek karo.

**Tools**: `gcc -Wall -Wextra` bahut se bugs compile time par pakad leta hai. `-g` ke saath build karke `gdb` mein step-by-step chalao. `-fsanitize=address` ya `valgrind` out-of-bounds aur leaks pakadte hain.

**Debugging habits**: pehle bug ko baar-baar reproduce karo, phir input chhota karo. Shak wali jagah `printf` se values dekho (`stderr` par, ya `fflush` ke saath). Return values (`fopen`, `malloc`, `scanf`) check karo. Ek baar mein ek hi change karo.

example.problem: Yeh function array ka maximum dena chahiye, par `{-5, -2, -9}` ke liye 0 deta hai. Bug dhoondho aur theek karo.
steps: Trace: `max = 0` se shuru. −5 > 0? Nahi. −2 > 0? Nahi. −9 > 0? Nahi. Return 0.
Bug: max ko 0 se shuru kiya, jo array mein hai hi nahi. Saare numbers negative hon to max kabhi update nahi hota.
Fix: `max = a[0]` se shuru karo aur loop index 1 se chalao.
Naya trace: max = −5; −2 > −5, to max = −2; −9 > −2? Nahi.
Answer: fixed function **−2** deta hai. Sabak: initial value hamesha data se lo.

mistakes: Compiler warnings ko ignore karna. `-Wall` ki zyada tar warnings asli bugs hoti hain (`=` in condition, unused value, missing return); unhe zero karo.
UB wale code ka output "maan" lena kyunki ek baar chal gaya. Doosri machine ya `-O2` par result badal sakta hai.
Bina soche bahut saare changes ek saath karna. Phir pata nahi chalta kis change ne bug theek kiya ya naya bug laaya.
revision: Trace table: har variable ka column, har line/round ki row.
n elements: index 0 se n − 1; loop `i < n`.
`if (...);` aur `for (...);` ka semicolon body ko alag kar deta hai.
UB ka output predict nahi karte; code theek karte hain.
`-Wall -Wextra -g` aur sanitizers ko aadat banao.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `for (...)` ke baad `;` ka matlab hai loop ki body khaali hai. Loop sirf i ko 0 se 5 tak badhata hai. Phir `s += i` (jo indentation se loop ka hissa dikhta hai) sirf ek baar chalta hai: s = 5. Trap: 10, indentation dekh kar sochna ki 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 jud raha hai.

questions.question: Is code mein kya bug hai?
options: a[0] chhoot jaata hai aur a[5] (array ke bahar) padha jaata hai
questions.explanation: Valid indices 0 se 4 hain. Loop 1 se 5 tak chalta hai, to `a[0]` (value 1) kabhi nahi judta, aur `a[5]` array ke bahar hai, jise padhna undefined behaviour hai. Compiler isse rokta nahi. Fix: `for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)`. Trap: "koi bug nahi", maths ki tarah 1 se 5 tak ginna.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: "Debug" mein lowercase letters e, b, u, g hain, 'D' capital hai, to n = 4. `s[4]` paanchwa character hai (index 0 se): D-0, e-1, b-2, u-3, g-4, to 'g'. Output "4 g". Trap: "4 u", index ko 1 se ginna; "5 g", capital 'D' ko bhi gin lena.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `85 / 10` integer division hai = 8, to `case 8` match hota hai: "B". Wahan `break` nahi, to fall-through se `case 7` ka "C", phir `break`. Output "BC". Trap: "B", break ki kami na dekhna; "ABC", yeh sochna ki switch upar ke cases bhi chalata hai.

questions.question: Is program ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Pehli call: calls = 1, v = 1 · 2 = 2, return 1 + 2 = 3. Doosri call: static calls ab 2, v = 2 · 2 = 4, return 2 + 4 = 6. v pointer se badla, to main mein v = 4. Output "3 6 4". Trap: "3 5 4", static ko har call par reset maan lena (1 + 4); "3 6 2", pointer se hua badlav bhool jaana.

questions.question: 64-bit Linux gcc par (int 4 bytes, ASCII) is program ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Loop ke baad: items[0] = ("A", 10), items[1] = ("B", 20), items[2] = ("C", 30). p = items + 1, to `p->val += items[2].val` se items[1].val = 20 + 30 = 50. `p++` ek poora Item aage, yaani items[2], to `p->tag` = "C". `sizeof(Item)` = 4 (char array) + 4 (int) = 8, koi padding nahi. Output "C 50 8". Trap: "B 50 8", `p++` bhool jaana; "C 20 8", yeh sochna ki p se badalne par items[1] nahi badla; "C 50 5", tag ko 1 byte ka maan lena.

questions.question: Array ke bahar padhna/likhna aur memory leaks run time par pakadne ke liye kaunsa tool use karte hain?
questions.explanation: AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address` ke saath build) aur valgrind program chalte waqt out-of-bounds access, use-after-free aur leaks pakadte hain. Trap: `-O2` sirf optimisation hai (bugs chhup bhi sakte hain); `gcc -E` sirf preprocessing dikhata hai.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `done / total` dono int hain: 3 / 4 = 0 (fraction kat gaya). Phir 0 double mein 0.0 banta hai: "0.00". Yeh aam bug hai; `(double)done / total` likho to 0.75 milega. Trap: 0.75, sochna ki double variable mein store karne se division double ho jaata hai; 1.00, round karna.

questions.question: In mein se kaunsa statement undefined behaviour hai?
questions.explanation: `i = i++;` ek hi expression mein i ko do baar badalta hai (assignment aur `++`), jo UB hai; compiler kuch bhi result de sakta hai. Baaki teeno i ko ek hi baar badalte hain aur sab 1 jodte hain. Trap: `++i;` ko bhi khatarnak samajhna; akele statement mein woh bilkul safe hai.

questions.question: Loop kitni baar chalega, yaani kya print hoga?
questions.explanation: i ki values: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, sab `>= 0` hain, to 6 rounds. Agla i = −2 par loop rukta hai. Trap: 5, 0 wala round bhool jaana (`>=` mein 0 bhi shaamil hai); 11, `i -= 2` ko `i--` samajhna.

questions.question: Is function mein kya bug hai?
options: `i <= n` ki wajah se loop ek round zyada chalta hai
s initialise nahi hua, to result garbage (UB) hai
Function ka return type void hona chahiye tha
Koi bug nahi; sum_to(4) hamesha 10 return karega
questions.explanation: Local variable `s` ki koi starting value nahi hai, usme garbage hai, aur `s += i` usi garbage mein jodta hai. Uninitialised value padhna UB hai. Fix: `int s = 0;`. Trap: "hamesha 10", kabhi-kabhi stack par 0 pada ho to sahi answer aa jaata hai, par yeh guarantee nahi; `i <= n` yahan sahi hai, kyunki 1 se n tak jodna hai.

questions.question: Trace table bana kar batao, is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Har round (t, a, b): i=0: (2, 1, 2), i=1: (3, 2, 3), i=2: (5, 3, 5), i=3: (8, 5, 8), i=4: (13, 8, 13). Loop 0 se 4 tak, yaani 5 baar. Output "8 13". Trap: "5 8", 4 hi rounds ginna; "13 21", 6 rounds; "13 13", `a = b` aur `b = t` ki order ulti kar dena.

questions.question: Yeh function compile karne par kya hoga?
options: Compile ho jaayega, par hamesha 0 return karega
Compile hoga, par a[n] (array ke bahar) check karega: UB
Compile error: neeche ke block mein `i` undeclared hai
Sahi kaam karega; `;` ka koi asar nahi padta
questions.explanation: `for (...);` ke baad ka `;` loop ki poori (khaali) body hai. `for` mein declared `i` ka scope usi loop statement tak hai, to neeche ke `{ }` block mein `i` exist hi nahi karta: compile error. Trap: a[n] wala option, yeh tab hota jab `i` loop ke bahar declare hota (jaise C89 style); "koi asar nahi", stray semicolon ko ignore karna.

questions.question: Int 4 bytes maan kar, is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Loop best ko sabse bade element par le jaata hai: 9, jo index 3 par hai. `best - data` = 3 (elements). `*best = 0` asal array mein data[3] ko 0 bana deta hai. data[1] = 8 waise hi hai. Trap: 9, index ki jagah value; "3 9 8", sochna ki pointer se likhne par array nahi badalta; 12, difference ko bytes mein ginna.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Switch ke andar ka `break` sirf switch se nikalta hai, loop se nahi. i = 0: s = 1. i = 1: case 1 se +10, break nahi to default mein +100: s = 111. i = 2: default +100: s = 211 > 200, ab loop wala `break`, i = 2 par. Trap: "1 0", sochna ki switch ka break loop bhi tod deta hai; "211 3", break ke baad i++ chala dena; "222 5", case 1 ka fall-through bhool jaana.
